problem.text: In rectangle $PQRS$, $PQ=8$ and $QR=6$. Points $A$ and $B$ lie on $\overline{PQ}$, points $C$ and $D$ lie on $\overline{QR}$, points $E$ and $F$ lie on $\overline{RS}$, and points $G$ and $H$ lie on $\overline{SP}$ so that $AP=BQ<4$ and the convex octagon $ABCDEFGH$ is equilateral. The length of a side of this octagon can be expressed in the form $k+m\sqrt{n}$, where $k$, $m$, and $n$ are integers and $n$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is $k+m+n$?

steps.title: Where to start: the octagon is the rectangle minus four corner triangles
steps.body: The octagon is what is left after cutting a right triangle off each corner of the rectangle. So name the legs of those triangles and write every side of the octagon in terms of them. Let $s$ be the side of the octagon and $x=AP=BQ$.

your_turn.prompt: Write the side $AB$ in terms of $x$.

steps.title: All four corners match
steps.body:
The corner triangles at $P$ and $Q$ share leg $x$ and hypotenuse $s$, so their other legs match too: $PH=QC$, which we call $y$. Then $CD=6-y-DR$ and $GH=6-y-SG$ both equal $s$, so $DR=SG$, and the corners at $R$ and $S$ match each other; since $EF=8-2\cdot RE=s=8-2x$, we get $RE=x$ and then $DR=y$. So all four corner triangles have legs $x$ (along the length-$8$ sides) and $y$ (along the length-$6$ sides):
$$s=8-2x=6-2y,\qquad s^2=x^2+y^2.$$

your_turn.prompt: Solve the first two equations for $x$ and $y$ in terms of $s$.

steps.title: One equation in $s$
steps.body:
Put these into $s^2=x^2+y^2$ and multiply both sides by $4$ to clear the fractions:
$$4s^2=(8-s)^2+(6-s)^2.$$

your_turn.prompt: Expand and simplify this into a quadratic equation with leading coefficient $1$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The quadratic formula gives $s=-7\pm\sqrt{49+50}=-7\pm\sqrt{99}=-7\pm3\sqrt{11}$. Careful: a side length is positive, so take $s=-7+3\sqrt{11}\approx2.95$ (then $x\approx2.5<4$, as required), not $-7-3\sqrt{11}$. Also careful: $k$ is $-7$, not $7$. So $k+m+n=-7+3+11=7$. The answer is **(B)**.

wrong_choices.A: This comes from the negative root $-7-3\sqrt{11}$, giving $-7-3+11=1$. A side length must be positive.
wrong_choices.C: This comes from dropping the minus sign on $k$ and adding $7+3+11=21$. In $-7+3\sqrt{11}$, $k=-7$.
